title: SDK Parity Matrix v2 (post-review) — Python / TypeScript / Go
content:
Redwood Inference — SDK parity audit
Matrix version: v2 (post-review)
Last review syncs: Platform/Gateway (Ethan/Amara/Brian), SRE (Rafael/Tomáš), Security (Marcus/Kevin/Aisha)
Primary goal of v2: lock target behaviors + call out *intentional deviations* and why.

Legend
- ✅ = matches target
- ⚠️ = partially matches / edge cases outstanding
- ❌ = does not match target
- (ID) = intentional deviation (accepted)

High-level decisions captured in v2
1) Retries are ON by default for safe classes (ADR-0137) but bounded by retry budget + jitter to prevent retry storms.
2) Streaming disconnects are *not transparently retried* by default (ADR-0138). SDKs surface a typed StreamingDisconnect error with request-id and bytes/events received so callers can decide.
3) Auth: single canonical header and env var order; no reading keys from arbitrary files by default (Security). Explicit opt-in for file-based key loading only where needed for enterprise (and must be documented + redacted).
4) Timeouts: provide consistent knobs across SDKs (connect / read / overall) with streaming-specific defaults.
5) Request ID: always propagate request-id from response headers into errors and optional logging hooks. Never log API keys.


SECTION A — Authentication + key handling
| Area | Python (pre-v2) | TypeScript (pre-v2) | Go (pre-v2) | Target behavior (post-review) | Decision / notes | Status | Owner / tracking |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API key discovery order | env var only (REDWOOD_API_KEY); some examples used REDWOOD_TOKEN | env var + constructor param; ambiguous docs about "token" | env var + optional config struct; env var name inconsistent in older examples | Order: (1) explicit per-client config (constructor) (2) env var REDWOOD_API_KEY (3) env var REDWOOD_TOKEN (deprecated alias) (4) shared config file path only if explicitly provided by caller | Security requested no implicit file reads. REDWOOD_TOKEN supported for 1 release cycle as alias w/ deprecation warning. | ⚠️ (alias/deprecation in flight) | ENG-2484; Docs ENG-2491 |
| Auth header | Authorization: Bearer <key> | Authorization: Bearer <key> (some older examples used X-API-Key) | X-API-Key (historical), some used Authorization | Canonical: Authorization: Bearer <key>. X-API-Key NOT sent by SDKs. | Platform/Gateway confirmed Bearer supported consistently across endpoints and regions. | ✅ | PRs: py#414 ts#290 go#201 |
| Header casing normalization | relies on requests/httpx default | varies by runtime (fetch/undici) | http.Header canonicalization | Must be semantically identical; do not assert on casing in tests | Conformance tests should treat header keys case-insensitively. | ✅ | ENG-2485 |
| Missing key error messaging | generic "Unauthorized" in some paths; sometimes thrown late | sometimes throws on first request; message inconsistent | sometimes returns error on request build | SDK should fail fast at client creation if key missing *unless* caller explicitly requests "lazy auth". Error should include remediation snippet (env var name) but never show key. | Security requested remediation guidance without leaking secrets. | ⚠️ | PRs: py#414 ts#290 go#201; Jira SUP-9355 |
| Invalid key / 401 handling | returned as generic APIError | mapped to generic error | mapped to error w/ status | Unified: AuthenticationError (status 401) with request-id, code if present, and redacted headers. No retries. | No retries for 401/403. | ✅ | ENG-2489 |
| 403 / org restrictions | generic | generic | generic | AuthorizationError (status 403) distinct from 401 | Improves enterprise triage. | ⚠️ | ENG-2489 |
| Secret redaction (logs/errors) | inconsistent in debug logs | inconsistent in thrown errors when request debug enabled | could log headers in verbose mode | Never log Authorization header. If debug logging is enabled, log only "Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]". Also redact any query params named key/token. | Security hard requirement. | ⚠️ | Security confluence note; PRs in progress |
| Multi-tenant apps | no clear guidance | no clear guidance | no clear guidance | Guidance: create one client per tenant key; do not swap global env vars at runtime; provide per-request override only if strongly needed (and mark as advanced). | Product + Security aligned; docs update required. | ⚠️ | Docs: redwood-docs#904 |

Intentional deviations (Auth)
- (ID-A1) Go: client creation may not "fail fast" when constructed with an empty config struct if caller intends to set key later. We will keep a strict default constructor that validates, and an explicit Advanced/Lazy constructor for advanced use cases.
- (ID-A2) TypeScript in browser: cannot rely on env vars. TS SDK will support explicit key only in browser builds; env var resolution documented as Node-only.


SECTION B — Retries + backoff + budgets
| Area | Python (pre-v2) | TypeScript (pre-v2) | Go (pre-v2) | Target behavior (post-review) | Decision / notes | Status | Owner / tracking |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Default retries enabled | mixed (some endpoints none) | enabled and sometimes aggressive | minimal | Enabled by default for safe classes with bounded attempts + retry budget | SRE requested explicit budget + jitter to prevent amplification. | ⚠️ | ADR-0137; ENG-2482 |
| Retryable HTTP status codes | 429, 500-599 (inconsistently) | 429, 500-599, sometimes 408 | some 5xx only | Retryable by default: 429, 500, 502, 503, 504. Not retryable: 400/401/403/404/409/422. 408 is NOT retried by default (edge-case: proxies). | Platform: 409 may be used for idempotency conflicts; do not retry by default. SRE: keep set conservative. | ✅ | PRs: py#412 ts#287 go#198 |
| Transport errors | some retried, some surfaced | varied by undici/fetch; some treated as retryable always | context cancellation sometimes misclassified | Retryable transport errors: connection reset, TLS handshake transient, EOF before response headers. Not retryable: DNS NXDOMAIN, invalid cert, context cancel, caller abort. | TS had retry storms on 429 due to misclassifying some errors + missing budget (SUP-9334). | ⚠️ | PRs: ts#287; go#198; Jira SUP-9334 |
| Backoff strategy | exp backoff (not consistent) | exp but jitter missing in some paths | fixed/backoff inconsistent | Exponential backoff w/ full jitter. Honor Retry-After if present (seconds or HTTP date) with ceiling. | Gateway adding Retry-After consistency (platform#18342). | ⚠️ | ADR-0137; platform#18342 |
| Max attempts | unclear | too high in some configs | low | Default max attempts: 3 total attempts (1 initial + up to 2 retries). Override allowed. | SRE recommended 3 total to limit blast radius. | ✅ | PRs: py#412 ts#287 go#198 |
| Retry budget | none | none | none | Per request: max additional time spent retrying = min(10s, overall_timeout * 0.5). If no overall_timeout, hard cap 10s. | Keeps behavior predictable across endpoints. | ⚠️ | ENG-2482; PRs in progress |
| Idempotency awareness | none | none | none | SDK will only auto-retry requests that are safe by method + endpoint classification. For POST generate/chat: retry allowed ONLY if request is explicitly idempotent (idempotency key set) OR if failure occurred before bytes sent (connect failure). | Aligns with client-retry-and-idempotency guidelines. | ⚠️ | ENG-2482; ENG-2490 |
| Rate limit interaction | ignores Retry-After | ignores Retry-After | partial | If 429 includes Retry-After, must wait at least that long before retry; if not present, use backoff. | Prevents extended throttling. | ⚠️ | platform#18342; Jira SUP-9334 |
| Retry telemetry hooks | none | some ad-hoc logging | none | Optional hooks: onRetry(attempt, delayMs, reason, requestId), onFinalError(err). Default off. | Observability advisors requested hook interface but not on by default. | ⚠️ | ENG-2490; Logan/Nadia review |

Intentional deviations (Retries)
- (ID-R1) TypeScript runtime differences: error types differ between undici and fetch (Node vs edge runtimes). TS SDK will normalize into a single RetryableTransportError classification but raw cause may differ; conformance asserts on classification, not exact message.
- (ID-R2) Go: if caller passes context with deadline < computed retry delays, Go SDK will stop retrying early and return context deadline exceeded. This is accepted and documented as "caller context always wins".


SECTION C — Timeouts
| Area | Python (pre-v2) | TypeScript (pre-v2) | Go (pre-v2) | Target behavior (post-review) | Decision / notes | Status | Owner / tracking |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Connect timeout default | inconsistent (varies by transport) | none by default in some environments | depends on http.Client | Default connect timeout: 10s non-streaming; 10s streaming | Customer reports of "hang" were usually missing read/overall timeouts + proxy buffering (SUP-9321). | ⚠️ | py#413 ts#288 go#199 |
| Read timeout default (non-stream) | sometimes unlimited | sometimes unlimited | sometimes unlimited | Default read timeout: 60s non-streaming | Gives predictable failure mode. | ⚠️ | ENG-2489; PRs above |
| Overall timeout default | none | none | none | Default overall timeout: 90s non-streaming, 0 (disabled) for streaming but require an explicit per-event read timeout | Streaming overall is tricky; see streaming section. | ⚠️ | ADR-0138; py#413 ts#288 go#199 |
| Streaming read timeout | none or too long | inconsistent | inconsistent | Default streaming "event gap" timeout: 30s (if no event bytes received within 30s, close + surface StreamingTimeout). | SRE: needed to avoid infinite hangs behind proxies. | ⚠️ | SUP-9321; ENG-2483 |
| Timeout error types | generic | generic | mixed with context cancel | Standardized: TimeoutError (overall), ConnectTimeoutError, ReadTimeoutError/StreamingTimeoutError. Each includes request-id (if available) and whether any bytes were received. | Helps support triage and customer handling. | ⚠️ | ENG-2489 |

Intentional deviations (Timeouts)
- (ID-T1) TypeScript in browsers/edge: cannot reliably implement separate connect vs read timeouts across all runtimes. TS SDK will expose a single "overall" timeout plus AbortSignal; connect/read split is best-effort Node-only.


SECTION D — Streaming (SSE) semantics + disconnect handling
| Area | Python (pre-v2) | TypeScript (pre-v2) | Go (pre-v2) | Target behavior (post-review) | Decision / notes | Status | Owner / tracking |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SSE framing parser | some partial-frame issues | issues with partial frames + proxy buffering | partial read handling issues | Must handle partial frames, multiple events per chunk, CRLF differences. Ignore unknown fields. | Conformance harness to include partial frame fixtures. | ⚠️ | py#415 ts#289 go#200; ENG-2485 |
| Event types | mixed naming | mixed | mixed | Standard: "message" events with JSON payload; terminal event "done"; tolerate server sending "error" event (rare). | Gateway team aligning payload consistency (platform#18343). | ⚠️ | platform#18343 |
| Cancellation | keyboard interrupt / cancel not consistent | AbortController supported | context cancel supported but not deterministic shutdown | Standard: cancellation must stop reading immediately, close body/stream, and return CancellationError (distinct from timeout). No retries. | Go needed deterministic shutdown for callers. | ⚠️ | ADR-0138; go#200; SUP-9342 |
| Mid-stream disconnect | sometimes retried implicitly | sometimes silently ends stream | surfaced as generic error | Default: do NOT auto-retry mid-stream. Surface StreamingDisconnect with: received_event_count, last_event_id (if present), request-id, retryable=false by default. | Avoid duplicating tokens / inconsistent app state. Caller may implement resume if their app protocol supports it. | ⚠️ | ADR-0138; TS support escalations (Slack + SUP tickets) |
| Safe resume guidance | none | none | none | Docs: recommend application-level "stateful" resume only with explicit cursor/offset support; otherwise restart request. SDK does not implement resume. | Required for enterprise. | ⚠️ | redwood-docs#904; quickstarts#233 |
| Per-event structured errors | inconsistent | inconsistent | inconsistent | If "error" event occurs, map to APIError with code/message + request-id, stop stream. | Align with unified error taxonomy. | ⚠️ | ENG-2489 |

Intentional deviations (Streaming)
- (ID-S1) TypeScript: AbortController semantics differ across runtimes; in some cases the fetch promise rejects with a DOMException name=AbortError. SDK will map these to CancellationError but raw cause differs.
- (ID-S2) Python: generator cancellation may surface as GeneratorExit/CancelledError depending on event loop/transport. SDK will normalize to CancellationError but may preserve original exception as "cause".


SECTION E — Error taxonomy + request-id propagation
| Area | Python (pre-v2) | TypeScript (pre-v2) | Go (pre-v2) | Target behavior (post-review) | Decision / notes | Status | Owner / tracking |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| request-id capture | sometimes dropped | sometimes dropped | often present | Always include request-id in returned response metadata and in errors (when available). | Gateway guarantees request-id header (platform#18342). | ⚠️ | ENG-2490; platform#18342 |
| Retry exhaustion error | generic | generic | generic | RetryExhaustedError includes attempts, total_sleep_ms, last_error_type, request-id (if any). | Support wants consistent messaging. | ⚠️ | ENG-2489 |
| Rate limit error shape | not normalized | not normalized | not normalized | If 429 payload includes machine-readable fields (limit, remaining, reset), surface RateLimitError with those fields; else generic APIError. | Depends on platform#18343 rollout. | ⚠️ | platform#18343 |


Accepted deviations summary (short)
- Auth: TS browser builds require explicit key (no env var). Go may allow "lazy auth" only via explicit advanced constructor.
- Timeouts: TS cannot guarantee connect/read split in all runtimes; expose best-effort.
- Retries: Go will stop early if caller context deadline is sooner (context always wins).
- Streaming: cancellation raw error types vary by runtime, but SDK maps to canonical CancellationError.


Action items / next steps (post-review)
1) Close remaining ⚠️ items in each SDK and update conformance harness to assert on classifications, not exact raw exceptions. (ENG-2485)
2) Ensure Retry-After is honored across SDKs once platform#18342 lands everywhere; add integration test: 429 with Retry-After and request-id. (ENG-2482 + platform)
3) Finalize error taxonomy docs + migration guide sections for:
   - new error classes
   - retry defaults (especially for TS customers impacted by SUP-9334)
   - streaming disconnect behavior (no auto-retry) (ENG-2491)
4) Security sign-off checklist: verify no Authorization header leaks in debug logs, exceptions, or telemetry hooks. (Security confluence note)

Appendix: customer-reported symptoms mapped to matrix rows
- SUP-9334 (TS retry storms on 429): Retry budget + honoring Retry-After + max attempts cap; fixed in ts#287 + platform#18342.
- SUP-9321 (Python streaming hang): streaming event gap timeout + clearer timeout defaults; py#413/#415.
- SUP-9342 (Go timeout vs context cancel confusion): explicit CancellationError vs TimeoutError mapping; go#199/#200.
- SUP-9355 (auth error unclear): fail-fast and remediation messaging; py#414 ts#290 go#201.
